items.title: Short-term headwind? Yes. But the structure stays intact: 5 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 19%
items.description: Wise men on the street will tell you it is foolish to try and time the market. And attempting to do so in the midst of a raging war is probably even more foolhardy. But even in these uncertain times, there is something that can be said with certainty: This war will also end. So, think beyond war, even as it rages on. Think of the structural stories that are changing some sectors.

items.title: Weekly Market Outlook: Can Nifty find its footing as crude, Fed policy drive markets?
items.description: Indian equities enter a holiday-shortened week with the Nifty at a crucial support zone after five consecutive weekly declines. The US Fed’s policy decision, FOMC projections, crude oil prices, global bond yields and foreign flows will drive near-term sentiment. Analysts expect volatility to remain elevated but see scope for buying at lower levels, with the Nifty’s 23,000–23,300 zone in focus.

items.title: EV-related stocks: Own the chain, not the guess; 13 stocks with upside potential of up to 28% and downside risk of -14%, according to analysts
items.description: In the stock market, when a big theme or sectoral trend takes off, most investors focus on the face of it. A brand with which they can relate. The same is happening in the auto sector, which is transitioning to the EV age. However, behind every EV is a long, hidden chain of businesses. Chasing an obvious name means betting on just one stock. There is a better way. Check out Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, for price targets of over 4,000 listed stocks along with detailed company analysis focusing on five key components – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. SR+ Reports is a complimentary offering to ETPrime members.

items.title: Oriental Insurance hopes to turn corner in FY27 assisted by NSE stake dilution
items.description: Looking ahead, Oriental Insurance Company projects a profitable turnaround by 2026-27, facilitated by a planned stake dilution in the National Stock Exchange through an upcoming IPO. The company plans to offer close to 49.57 lakh shares in this process. Such a move is anticipated to enhance financial stability and liquidity, with subscriptions commencing on September 17, marking a key milestone for the insurer.

items.title: ETMarkets Smart Talk| From floor trading to AI algos: Why India’s retail traders are entering the automation era, says Shruti Jain
items.description: AI-powered algorithmic trading is becoming increasingly accessible to Indian retail investors, driven by Sebi’s regulatory framework, trading APIs and zero-code platforms. Arihant Capital’s Shruti Jain explains how automation can improve execution, reduce emotional bias and potentially become a mainstream trading habit.

items.title: 8 midcap stocks clock up to 245% EBITDA growth in June quarter. Do you own any?
items.description: Quarterly EBITDA growth indicates an increase in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation, providing an indicator of changes in profitability and operational performance. Within the NSE mid-cap segment, eight stocks reported EBITDA growth of more than 80% in the June 2026 quarter compared with the same period last year (excluding banking and financial stocks), according to StockEdge profitability data.

items.title: Dividends and stock splits: Hindustan Copper, Cochin Shipyard among 200+ stocks with record dates this week. Check full list
items.description: Over 90 companies have fixed September 18 as the record date for dividends and other corporate actions. Victoria Mills leads with a Rs 50 per share dividend, followed by Sharda Motor Industries at Rs 20. The list also includes several companies announcing dividends, while Oriana Power and Kairosoft Ai Solutions have set record dates for stock splits.

items.title: FPIs withdraw Rs 13,138 crore from equities in September so far amid global uncertainty
items.description: During the first week of September, a massive outflow of Rs 13,138 crore from Indian equities occurred, marking a stark reversal after foreign investors had previously engaged in net buying during July and August. The pullback can be attributed to global uncertainties, climbing crude oil costs, and rising US bond yields.

items.title: 11 penny stocks rose up to 156% in just 6 months. Do you own any?
items.description: Over the last six months, 11 penny stocks recorded returns ranging from 27% to 156%. These stocks were identified using a defined set of filters: market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price under Rs 20, and a minimum latest trading volume of 5 lakh shares. The screening criteria were used to identify low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks that had delivered strong upward price momentum. (Data Source: ACE Equity)
